newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Four Timorese enter Spanish embassy in Jakarta.
newsitem.headline: Four Timorese enter Spanish embassy in Jakarta.

text.p: Four East Timorese entered the Spanish embassy in Jakarta seeking political asylum on Tuesday and were expected to leave for Portugal later in the day, human rights lawyer Johannes Princen said.
Princen, director of the Institute for the Defence of Human Rights, told Reuters the four East Timorese had entered the embassy around 7 a.m. (midnight GMT).
"The problem will be solved tonight. They are going to Portugal, probably," he said.
An Indonesian Foreign Ministry spokesman said the government was aware that the East Timorese were in the mission.
"We are aware of them in the Spanish embassy...we have no objection to them leaving the country," he said.
An official at the embassy said she was unable to comment and referred all questions to the Foreign Ministry in Madrid.
Henri Fournier, head of the Jakarta office of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), said the ICRC had been contacted about the East Timorese and was taking "appropriate steps".

One of the four was believed to have entered the French embassy on October 16 with two colleagues. The three, who were seen in the embassy by Reuter reporters, were expelled later in the day by embassy guards.
Five East Timorese entered the Spanish embassy in September and spent two weeks there before leaving for asylum in Portugal on September 24.
A total of 89 East Timorese, not including the latest four, have been granted asylum in Portugal since the latest series of break-ins into foreign missions in Jakarta started in September last year.

Students at the University of East Timor staged a brief protest in front of the campus on Tuesday on the fifth anniversary of the killing of at least 50 demonstrators by Indonesian troops in the capital Dili.

Indonesian troops killed 50 demonstrators in 1991 following a funeral for an anti-Indonesian activist in Dili, according to an official report. Witnesses and human rights groups estimated at least 180 people died and many were injured.
Indonesian troops invaded the eastern, former Portuguese, half of Timor island in December 1975 and proclaimed it as its 27th province the following July.
The United Nations has refused to recognise Indonesian sovereignty over the territory, which has posed a recurring problem for Jakarta in its international relations over the past 20 years.
